affiliations.role_title: First lieutenant; later lieutenant colonel, Corps of Engineers, assistant chief of staff G-1
affiliations.date_precision: Contemporary Indiana rosters document first-lieutenant service in 1922 and lieutenant-colonel engineer staff service in 1938; they do not prove uninterrupted service or an immediate OSS transfer.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact rare name and middle initials recur in the OSS index and two Indiana military rosters. The reviewed sources establish prewar military affiliation, not a civilian employer or immediate OSS predecessor.

affiliations.date_precision: The scholarly account says Skarzynski escaped to join the French Army and was then recruited by OSS in Paris; Operation Ruppert was proposed in October 1944.
affiliations.research_notes: A scholarly source citing the underlying NARA mission file explicitly places French Army service before OSS recruitment. The NARA awards memorandum independently confirms the distinctive OSS identity and stateless-civilian status.

affiliations.date_precision: A contemporary Harvard newspaper identifies Skerpan as an upperclass scholarship recipient in November 1934; an Air University biography confirms his Harvard A.B. before OSS service beginning in 1942.
affiliations.research_notes: Harvard is published only as student status. It is not classified as an employer, and the reviewed sources do not establish Skerpan's immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
